report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Probe definitions: arrival, instruction, anchoring, comprehension, and the ProbeSpec registry.

symbols.name: _SUMMARY_DECOYS
symbols.note: Tuple of six decoy one-line summaries, used in comprehension probe.

symbols.name: _SUMMARY_TARGETS
symbols.note: Tuple of three rollback-related target summaries.

symbols.name: _filler
symbols.note: Generates pad_lines lines of random padding words using the given RNG.

symbols.name: ARRIVAL_PAD_LINES
symbols.note: Default padding line count for arrival probe, set to 40.

symbols.name: build_arrival
symbols.note: Builds arrival probe prompt with NONCE-<nonce> at start and TAILWORD: <tail> at end, with filler between.

symbols.name: expect_arrival
symbols.note: Returns expected arrival reply: 'NONCE-<nonce> <tail>'.

symbols.name: check_arrival
symbols.note: Checks reply contains both head token and tail word; returns (bool, reason).

symbols.name: _FENCE_RE
symbols.note: Compiled regex to strip leading/trailing code fences.

symbols.name: build_instruction
symbols.note: Builds instruction probe prompt asking for exactly OK-<nonce>.

symbols.name: expect_instruction
symbols.note: Returns expected instruction reply: 'OK-<nonce>'.

symbols.name: _normalise
symbols.note: Strips transport artefacts: fences, surrounding quotes, whitespace, trailing periods.

symbols.name: check_instruction
symbols.note: Checks reply exactly equals expected; distinguishes not_exact vs answer_absent.

symbols.name: _anchor_pair
symbols.note: Generates (prompt_body, decoy, correct) for anchoring probe.

symbols.name: build_anchoring
symbols.note: Builds anchoring probe prompt via _anchor_pair.

symbols.name: expect_anchoring
symbols.note: Returns correct answer for anchoring probe via _anchor_pair.

symbols.name: check_anchoring
symbols.note: Checks reply for decoy/correct word; returns anchored_on_decoy, wrong_word, or success.

symbols.name: _NUMBER_WORDS
symbols.note: Mapping of number words to digits for comprehension probe.

symbols.name: _NUMBER_RE
symbols.note: Regex to match digits or number words.

symbols.name: _summaries
symbols.note: Generates list of three summaries with one target and returns (lines, target_number).

symbols.name: build_comprehension
symbols.note: Builds comprehension probe prompt with three numbered summaries.

symbols.name: expect_comprehension
symbols.note: Returns expected comprehension answer as string of target number.

symbols.name: check_comprehension
symbols.note: Checks reply for number matching target; returns no_number, wrong_number, or success.

symbols.name: ProbeSpec
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass defining a probe with name, severity, build, check, expect, blurb.

symbols.name: PROBES
symbols.note: Tuple of ProbeSpec instances for arrival and instruction probes (anchoring truncated at end).

claims.text: ~40 lines of filler is roughly 800 tokens: long enough that a transport which truncates has something to truncate, and far enough under the Ollama usable input window that the probe itself never provokes the failure it measures.
claims.why: The claim about token count and Ollama window size depends on external tokenization and model limits not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Both incidents were truncation, in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, so one token cannot catch both: * Ollama HEAD-truncates an over-budget prompt (it eats the system prompt first), so the HEAD token disappears; * the npm .cmd shim cut a multi-line argv at the first newline, so the TAIL -- including the instruction telling the model what to do -- disappeared, and the model answered 'your message was cut off'.
claims.why: The claim describes historical incidents and external behaviour (Ollama, npm shim) not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: Requiring BOTH tokens back is what makes a single cheap probe cover both. It also closes the obvious false pass: a model that lost the tail may still echo the head token while complaining about the cut, and that reply is correctly rejected because it cannot contain a tail word it never received.
claims.why: check_arrival requires both head and tail; if tail missing, returns tailword_absent even if head present, preventing false pass.

claims.text: Accept only if BOTH ends of the prompt demonstrably arrived.
claims.why: check_arrival checks head_ok and tail_ok; only returns True if both true.

claims.text: Strip TRANSPORT artefacts only -- never content. Code fences, surrounding quotes and stray whitespace are things a CLI wrapper adds; removing them keeps the probe measuring instruction-following rather than punishing a lane for its own output framing. Anything the model actually chose to say survives this and is judged.
claims.why: _normalise only removes fences, surrounding quotes, whitespace, and trailing periods; does not remove other content.

claims.text: It knew the answer and said more anyway. That is the degradation this probe exists for -- a lane that is alive and no longer obedient.
claims.why: If want in reply but not exact, returns not_exact.

claims.text: Detect a lane that copied the decoy instead of answering.
claims.why: If decoy present, returns anchored_on_decoy regardless of correct presence.

claims.text: Reported as a QUALITY signal by :data:`PROBES`: a model anchoring on a prior turn is alive, reachable and useless for reasoning work. Calling that a liveness failure would page someone about a model choice; calling it nothing is how it went unnoticed for a day.
claims.why: The severity classification and PROBES registry are partially defined here; anchoring is not yet in PROBES in this chunk, and the historical incident is external.

claims.text: The nonce is deliberately NOT in this prompt: the answer is a digit, and a nonce full of digits would give a lazy checker something to trip over.
claims.why: build_comprehension does not include nonce in prompt; it only uses summaries.

claims.text: A tiny real task with a checkable answer.
claims.why: The prompt asks to identify which summary mentions rollback, with a deterministic answer.

claims.text: A probe is (prompt, checker) and the checker is deterministic Python.
claims.why: ProbeSpec holds build, check, expect; check functions are deterministic given nonce.

observations.what: check_arrival uses regex with re.IGNORECASE for tail word, but head token is case-sensitive.

check_instruction checks want in (reply or '') before normalisation, but the not_exact branch only triggers if the raw reply contains the wanted string; if the normalised text differs but raw contains it, it returns not_exact.
_normalise strips trailing periods but not other punctuation; this could affect exact match for instruction probe if model adds a period after OK-<nonce>.
check_comprehension uses _NUMBER_RE.search on raw reply; if reply contains multiple numbers, it takes the first, which may not be the intended answer.

_summaries uses rng.sample(_SUMMARY_DECOYS, 3) which picks 3 distinct decoys; then replaces one with a target. The target is chosen from _SUMMARY_TARGETS which are all rollback-related, but the decoys are distinct and may also contain 'rollback'? Decoys are defined without 'rollback', so the target is the only one mentioning rollback.
PROBES tuple is truncated at the end of this chunk; anchoring probe is not yet included in the shown PROBES, but the docstring references it as part of PROBES.

risks: check_arrival | low | Head token case-sensitive but tail word case-insensitive; a model replying with lowercase nonce would fail head check. | Determine if nonce case should be normalised.
